findings.reason: a node built to §9 would implement a promoted-run release on the strength of an observation made almost entirely about dispatched pointers, and if no promoted claim is in that state the section repairs a path no promoted run takes; the author should either cite a promoted instance or fold the job-less liveness read into the run's liveness reader.
findings.text: §9 states that "47 of 76 live pointers carried a placement naming no readable job id" and concludes "A promoted run in that state keeps its claim however long its worker has been gone. Its cited record (docs/evidence/archive/a-claim-nobody-is-working-is-released-landed.html, line 74) reports that 47-of-76 count over the whole live-pointer population, whose own census summary puts 75 of the 76 in kind `dispatched` and one in kind `promoted`, and the record names no promoted pointer inside the 47; the one promoted pointer at that census is the run §8 already repairs as liveness-dead.

findings.reason: the dedupe is a stated behaviour the section turns on and no arm can fail it, so the gate would pass both a compliant one-report implementation and a per-pass one; the section needs the report's scope (once per run) written and an arm that runs a second pass and requires no second report.
findings.text: the deliverable requires an undecidable run to be "reported once as an obligation naming what is missing, rather than held without a word", but the done-when's third arm asks only that such a pointer "is reported as an obligation naming the missing fact", so a node that reports it on every pass satisfies the arm while defeating the deliverable's one-report requirement, and the done-when never fixes what "once" is counted over.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited record docs/evidence/archive/a-claim-nobody-is-working-is-released-landed.html exists and carries the named paragraph "An own-node run was not proved dead at that census" (line 74 of that file); the test path named is a file to create, not an anchor.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §9's obligation arm (docs/plans/a-claim-nobody-is-working-is-released.html:93-94) requires an undecidable run to be "reported once", but no arm distinguishes one report across repeated passes from a report on every pass, and "once" is not scoped.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §9 puts each arm's log under the section's run directory (docs/plans/a-claim-nobody-is-working-is-released.html:94), a durable path a later reader can open, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §9's test file and prose name the mechanism (a placement without a job is judged), with no plan label, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §9's stated cause for promoted claims rests on a population in which 75 of the 76 cited pointers are dispatched pointers, and the cited record names no promoted pointer among the 47.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9 carries one endpoint: decide liveness for a promoted pointer whose placement names no readable job id, with the undecidable case as its residual branch.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s9 is listed in §6's `plan-section-depends-on` (docs/plans/a-claim-nobody-is-working-is-released.html:24) and §9 introduces no dependency on a section it fails to declare.
